nodes.content: Develop tactile slip prediction that distinguishes impending grasp slip from elastic deformation across unseen materials and sensor wear.
requirements: Predict slip at least 100 milliseconds ahead with ≥90% recall and ≤5% false-positive rate.
Meet targets on held-out materials and worn sensors, including deformation-only contacts matched for force.

nodes.content: Train a wear-augmented, material-adversarial shear-field encoder to forecast slip 100 ms ahead from microslip against force-matched elastic negatives.
Do wear-attenuated shear precursors remain separable from force-matched elastic relaxation 100 ms before slip on unseen materials?
Shear residuals distinguish 100-ms-ahead slip from force-matched elastic relaxation on unseen materials and worn sensors at ≥90% recall, ≤5% FPR.
Collect WearSlip-12 force-matched deformation/slip trials; train the wear-augmented encoder, then measure 100-ms recall and FPR on held-out materials/sensors.
Evaluate the wear-augmented encoder on WearSlip-12's held-out materials and worn sensors, measuring 100-ms recall and force-matched deformation FPR.
On WearSlip-12 held-out materials and worn sensors, 100-ms recall reached 92%, but force-matched deformation FPR was 13%.
Wear-calibrated directional shear propagation will distinguish slip from elastic relaxation, reducing deformation FPR to ≤5% at ≥90% 100-ms recall.
Ablate wear-calibrated shear propagation against residual-only encoding on WearSlip-12 held-out materials and worn sensors; measure 100-ms recall and deformation FPR.
On WearSlip-12 held-out materials and worn sensors, calibrated propagation achieved 91% 100-ms recall and 4% deformation FPR, versus 92%/13% residual-only.
Retire residual-only after its initial held-out 13% deformation FPR; adopt calibrated propagation after ablation reaches 91% recall and 4% FPR.
Freeze the adopted calibrated-propagation model; run streaming WearSlip-12 trials across abrasion grades, logging 100-ms recall and force-matched deformation FPR.
WearSlip-12 Streaming Audit v1 contains frozen-model predictions, sensor-wear grades, held-out material IDs, and 100-ms recall and deformation FPR.
Can one fixed alert threshold maintain ≤5% deformation FPR across abrasion grades without per-sensor slip-label recalibration?
Select one threshold on unworn WearSlip-12 trials; audit abrasion-grade 100-ms recall and deformation FPR without recalibration.
Fixed unworn-selected threshold yielded ≥90% 100-ms recall and ≤5% force-matched deformation FPR at every abrasion grade on held-out materials.
Stress-test the fixed threshold on independent worn-sensor batches and unseen materials with force-matched relaxation; measure worst-grade 100-ms recall and FPR.
On unseen materials and independently worn sensors, fixed-threshold propagation yielded 87% 100-ms recall and 9% force-matched deformation FPR.
Audit WearSlip-12 Streaming Audit v1 for grade-wise threshold robustness and missing sensor-batch IDs needed to verify independent-wear performance.
WearSlip-12 Streaming Audit v1 records grade-wise ≥90% 100-ms recall and ≤5% FPR but omits batch IDs, obscuring independent-wear failures.
Retain calibrated propagation but defer deployment: grade-wise tests passed, yet batch IDs are missing and independent-wear performance fails both targets.
Train a batch-normalized 100-ms motion-ratio forecaster with conformal alert thresholds calibrated on force-matched deformation probes from each worn-sensor batch.
How many per-batch deformation probes preserve ≥90% 100-ms recall and ≤5% FPR on unseen materials and independently worn sensors?
Forty batch-specific force-matched deformation probes enable ≥90% 100-ms recall and ≤5% FPR on unseen materials and independently worn sensors.
Sweep 20/40/80 force-matched probes per batch; evaluate conformal 100-ms recall and FPR on unseen materials and independently worn sensors.
With 40 probes/batch, conformal motion ratios reached 91% 100-ms recall and 4% force-matched deformation FPR on independent-wear/unseen-material trials.
Advance 40-probe batch-calibrated motion ratios for validation: independent-wear trials achieved 91% 100-ms recall and 4% deformation FPR.
Fuse wear-normalized shear-wave coherence and contact-area strain hysteresis in a physics-constrained state-space model for 100-ms slip alerts.
Does strain hysteresis suppress deformation false alarms without masking early shear-wave coherence on worn sensors and unseen materials?
Adding strain hysteresis to shear-wave coherence reduces force-matched deformation FPR to ≤5% while retaining ≥90% recall at 100 ms.
Compare fused versus coherence-only state-space models on independent-wear, unseen-material, force-matched trials; measure 100-ms recall and deformation FPR.
On independent-wear/unseen-material trials, fusion achieved 4% force-matched deformation FPR versus 11% baseline, but 84% 100-ms recall versus 92%.
Condition hysteresis veto on spatially diffuse strain, preserving localized shear precursors at ≥90% 100-ms recall and ≤5% FPR.
Ablate diffuse-strain hysteresis veto against unconditional fusion on independent-wear/unseen-material contacts; measure 100-ms recall and force-matched deformation FPR.
Diffuse-strain veto restored 91% 100-ms recall with 5% force-matched deformation FPR, versus unconditional fusion’s 84% and 4%.
Stratify independent-wear trials by abrasion grade; test diffuse-strain veto for 100-ms recall and force-matched deformation FPR.
Severely abraded sensors yielded 86% 100-ms recall and 8% force-matched deformation FPR, despite pooled 91% recall and 5% FPR.
Abrasion-adaptive diffuse-strain veto thresholds restore ≥90% 100-ms recall and ≤5% force-matched deformation FPR on severely worn sensors.
Calibrate abrasion-adaptive veto thresholds on separate wear-characterization trials; evaluate independent severe-wear 100-ms recall and force-matched deformation FPR on unseen materials.
On independent severe-wear, unseen-material trials, abrasion-adaptive veto reached 91% 100-ms recall and 4% force-matched deformation FPR.
Freeze n40-validated adaptive veto thresholds; test new severe-wear batches on unseen materials with force-matched deformation, measuring 100-ms recall/FPR.
On new severe-wear batches and unseen materials, frozen adaptive veto yielded 88% 100-ms recall and 7% force-matched deformation FPR.
Per-batch quiet-contact normalization will stabilize diffuse-strain vetoes across severe-wear/unseen-material batches at ≥90% 100-ms recall and ≤5% deformation FPR.
Compare quiet-contact-normalized and abrasion-adaptive vetoes on new severe-wear batches and unseen materials; measure 100-ms recall and force-matched deformation FPR.
On new severe-wear batches and unseen materials, recalibrated abrasion-adaptive veto achieved 91% recall/4% FPR; quiet-contact normalization achieved 88%/7%.
Stratify quiet-contact-normalized alerts by strain localization and abrasion grade; quantify missed 100-ms shear precursors and force-matched deformation false alarms.
On unseen-material severe-wear trials, normalization achieved 93% 100-ms recall for localized precursors and 4% diffuse-deformation FPR.
Select recalibrated abrasion-adaptive veto (91% recall, 4% FPR); localized normalization gains cannot offset its overall 88%/7%.
Use subthreshold 30-Hz microdither and wear-normalized tangential impedance phase to predict slip 100 ms ahead versus elastic relaxation.
Does 30-Hz dither phase separate impending slip from force-matched viscoelastic relaxation without perturbing grasps across unseen materials and wear?
A 0.05-N, 30-Hz microdither yields ≥90% 100-ms slip recall and ≤5% deformation FPR with <1% induced grasp slips.
Run randomized dither/sham grasps across held-out materials and abrasion batches; assess 100-ms recall, force-matched deformation FPR, and induced-slip rate.
Randomize 0.05-N, 30-Hz dither versus sham across unseen-material, independent-wear grasps; measure 100-ms recall, deformation FPR, and induced-slip rate.
Across unseen materials and independently worn sensors, microdither achieved 92% 100-ms recall, 4% deformation FPR, and 0.4% induced slips.
Freeze the validated microdither configuration; stream new-batch grasps, logging 100-ms recall, force-matched deformation FPR, and induced-slip rate.
Microdither Streaming Audit v1 logs batch IDs, held-out materials, 100-ms slip alerts, force-matched deformation labels, and dither-induced slips.
Audit Microdither Streaming Audit v1 for batch completeness, unseen-material 100-ms recall, force-matched deformation FPR, and induced-slip rate.
Audit v1: complete batch IDs; new-batch unseen-material trials yielded 91% 100-ms recall, 4% force-matched deformation FPR, 0.6% induced slips.
Fuse contact-microphone stick-slip chirps with tactile shear via wear-robust cross-modal timing, training on force-matched elastic negatives for 100-ms forecasts.
Do microphone chirps synchronize with shear precursors 100 ms before slip, unlike force-matched elastic recoil across material and wear shifts?
Chirp–shear alignment within 12 ms yields ≥90% 100-ms slip recall and ≤5% deformation FPR on unseen materials and worn sensors.
Compare 12-ms chirp–shear alignment against shuffled timing on unseen-material, independent-wear trials; measure 100-ms recall and force-matched deformation FPR.
On unseen-material, independent-wear trials, 12-ms alignment yielded 93% 100-ms recall but 8% deformation FPR; shuffled timing yielded 12% FPR.
Compare 12-ms chirp–shear alignment in 100-ms pre-slip windows versus force-matched elastic recoil, stratified by damping and wear.
On low-damping unseen materials with worn sensors, 12-ms alignment achieved 92% 100-ms recall and 4% elastic-recoil FPR.
Damping-conditioned chirp–shear alignment suppresses viscoelastic recoil, achieving ≥90% 100-ms recall and ≤5% deformation FPR across material/wear shifts.
Train damping-conditioned chirp–shear alignment on separate materials; test 100-ms recall and force-matched deformation FPR across independent-wear batches.
Across unseen materials and independent-wear batches, damping-conditioned alignment achieved 91% 100-ms recall and 5% force-matched deformation FPR.
Freeze the n68 damping-conditioned model; evaluate new high-damping materials and worn-sensor batches for 100-ms recall and force-matched deformation FPR.
On new high-damping materials and worn-sensor batches, frozen alignment achieved 86% 100-ms recall and 9% force-matched deformation FPR.
Per-batch force-matched recoil-null calibration of chirp–shear likelihood ratios restores ≥90% 100-ms recall and ≤5% FPR on high-damping materials/worn sensors.
After frozen-model failure, calibrate chirp–shear ratios using batch-specific recoil-null probes; measure 100-ms recall/FPR on new high-damping materials and worn sensors.
With per-batch recoil-null calibration, high-damping trials reached 89% 100-ms recall and 6% force-matched deformation FPR.
Sweep 20/40/80 recoil-null probes per worn-sensor batch on high-damping materials; measure chirp–shear lag, 100-ms recall, and deformation FPR.
On high-damping unseen materials and worn sensors, 80 recoil-null probes/batch yielded 91% 100-ms recall and 4% deformation FPR.
Eighty recoil-null probes per worn-sensor batch calibrate chirp–shear ratios for ≥90% 100-ms recall and ≤5% FPR on unseen high-damping materials.
After 89%/6% initial calibration and 91%/4% with 80 probes, freeze the 80-probe protocol; test new high-damping materials and worn-sensor batches.
On new high-damping materials and independently worn batches, frozen 80-probe calibration achieved 90% 100-ms recall and 5% deformation FPR.
Advance 80-probe recoil-null calibration cautiously: 100-ms recall/FPR improved from 89%/6% to 91%/4%, then validated at 90%/5% independently.
Prospectively log 80-probe-calibrated chirp–shear lags in independent high-damping batches; compare pre-slip and force-matched recoil timing and 100-ms recall/FPR.
Prospectively compare 80-probe-calibrated chirp–shear lag before slip versus force-matched recoil across unseen high-damping materials and independent-wear batches; measure 100-ms recall/FPR.
Chirp–Shear Prospective Audit v1 contains 80-probe calibration logs, material and wear-batch IDs, pre-slip/recoil lags, and 100-ms recall/FPR.
